In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Alamedilla PETM record reflects the response of deep-sea foraminiferal assemblages to the global warming and major carbon cycle perturbation.
the Alamedilla PETM event is characterized by a rapid warming of ~6°C (at least 5°C) and a ~30% increase in atmospheric pCO2.
the Alamedilla PETM record is characterized by a rapid warming of the bottom waters and the surface waters, and a rapid and severe oxygen depletion of bottom waters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PETM is characterized by a major faunal turnover, with a strong decrease in the abundance of benthic foraminafifera and an increase in planktic species.
the ocean warming during the PETM was not a uniform event, but it was more intense at the upper bathyal–lower abyssal depths than at the upper abyssal depths.
the Alamedilla foraminiferal record shows a clear faunal turnover, with a dramatic extinction event of benthic forams, and the appearance and rapid evolutionary turnover of several planktic forams.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the foraminiferal assemblages are characterized by an increase in the abundance of species tolerant of low oxygen and high temperature conditions, and by a decrease of species sensitive to low oxygen and high temperatures.
the PETM is associated with a major reorganization of the benthic forminiferal community, with an increase in the relative abundance of small-sized species.
foraminiferal assemblages from the Alamedilla site are strongly affected by the global warming event, with the extinction of benthic forams and the turnover of planktic species.
